arxiv-1710-05406.title: Variable selection for (realistic) stochastic blockmodels
arxiv-1710-05406.creator: Mirko Signorelli
arxiv-1710-05406.description: Abstract Stochastic blockmodels provide a convenient representation of relations between communities of nodes in a network. However, they imply a notion of stochastic equivalence that is often unrealistic for real networks, and they comprise large number of parameters that can make them hardly interpretable.

arxiv-2102-06247.title: Sample-Optimal PAC Learning of Halfspaces with Malicious Noise
arxiv-2102-06247.creator: Jie Shen
arxiv-2102-06247.description: Abstract We study efficient PAC learning of homogeneous halfspaces in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} in the presence of malicious noise of Valiant (1985). This is a challenging noise model and only until recently has near-optimal noise tolerance bound been established under the mild condition that the unlabeled data distribution is isotropic log-concave.

arxiv-2103-00976.title: T-Singular Values and T-Sketching for Third Order Tensors
arxiv-2103-00976.creator: Liqun Qi, Gaohang Yu
arxiv-2103-00976.description: Abstract Based upon the T-SVD (tensor SVD) of third order tensors, introduced by Kilmer and her collaborators, we define T-singular values of third order tensors. T-singular values of third order tensors are nonnegative scalars. The number of nonzero T-singular values is the tensor tubal rank of the tensor.

arxiv-2305-07227.title: Multireference protonation energetics of a dimeric model of nitrogenase iron–sulfur clusters
arxiv-2305-07227.creator: Huanchen Zhai, Seunghoon Lee, Zhi-Hao Cui, Lili Cao, Ulf Ryde, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
arxiv-2305-07227.description: Abstract Characterizing the electronic structure of the iron–sulfur clusters in nitrogenase is necessary to understand their role in the nitrogen fixation process. One challenging task is to determine the protonation state of the intermediates in the nitrogen fixing cycle. Here, we use a dimeric iron–sulfur model to study relative energies of protonation at C, S or Fe.

arxiv-2307-10553.title: On the nature of slowly rising interaction-powered supernovae 2023 On the nature of slowly rising interaction-powered supernovae – References
arxiv-2307-10553.creator: Takashi J. Moriya
arxiv-2307-10553.description: Abstract Some interaction-powered supernovae have long rise times of more than 100 days. We show that such long rise times are naturally expected if circumstellar matters (CSM) have a flat density structure ( s ≲ 1.5 s\lesssim 1.5 , where ρ CSM ∝ r − s \rho_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto r^{-s} ).

arxiv-2402-16247.title: Learning Translations: Emergent Communication Pretraining for Cooperative Language Acquisition
arxiv-2402-16247.creator: Dylan Cope, Peter McBurney
arxiv-2402-16247.description: Abstract In Emergent Communication (EC) agents learn to communicate with one another, but the protocols that they develop are specialised to their training community. This observation led to research into Zero-Shot Coordination (ZSC) for learning communication strategies that are robust to agents not encountered during training.

arxiv-2410-04133.title: An Electrocardiogram Foundation Model Built on over 10 Million Recordings with External Evaluation across Multiple Domains
arxiv-2410-04133.creator: Jun Li, Aaron Aguirre, Junior Moura, Che Liu, Lanhai Zhong, Chenxi Sun, Gari Clifford, Brandon Westover, Shenda Hong
arxiv-2410-04133.description: Abstract BACKGROUND . Artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated significant potential in ECG analysis and cardiovascular disease assessment. Recently, foundation models have played a remarkable role in advancing medical AI, bringing benefits such as efficient disease diagnosis and cross-domain knowledge transfer. The development of an ECG foundation model holds the promise of elevating AI-ECG research to new heights.

arxiv-2410-10914.title: Towards Better Multi-head Attention via Channel-wise Sample Permutation
arxiv-2410-10914.creator: Shen Yuan, Hongteng Xu
arxiv-2410-10914.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shen Yuan, Hongteng Xu. Transformer plays a central role in many fundamental deep learning models, e.g., the ViT in computer vision and the BERT and GPT in natural language processing, whose effectiveness is mainly attributed to its multi-head attention (MHA) mechanism. In this study, we propose a simple and novel channel-wise sample permutation (CSP) operator, achieving a new structured MHA with fewer parameters and lower complexity.

arxiv-2502-19265.title: Unveiling What Makes Saturn Ring Quantifying the Amplitudes of Saturn’s Planetary Normal-mode Oscillations and trends in C-ring Properties using Kronoseismology (VII)
arxiv-2502-19265.creator: V. M. Afigbo, M. M. Hedman, P. D. Nicholson, R. G. French, C. R. Mankovich, R. G. Jerousek, J. Dewberry
arxiv-2502-19265.description: Abstract Certain spiral density waves in Saturn’s rings are generated through resonances with planetary normal modes, making them valuable probes of Saturn’s internal structure. Previous research has primarily focused on the rotation rates of these waves. However, other characteristics of these waves also contain valuable information about the planet’s interior.

arxiv-2509-04798.title: Distributed-HISQ : A Distributed Quantum Control Architecture Conference: 58th IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture; October 18–22, 2025; Seoul, Republic of Korea 58th IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture (MICRO ’25), October 18–22, 2025, Seoul, Republic of Korea DO
arxiv-2509-04798.creator: Yilun Zhao 2,3, Abstract. Kangding Zhao 1, Abstract. Peng Zhou 4 Dingdong Liu 1 Tingyu Luo 5 Yuzhen Zheng 1 Peng Luo 1 Shun Hu 1 Jin Lin 6,7 Cheng Guo 6 Yinhe Han 2 Ying Wang 2 Mingtang Deng 1 Junjie Wu 1 X. Fu 1, Abstract.
arxiv-2509-04798.description: Abstract . The design of a scalable Quantum Control Architecture (QCA) faces two primary challenges. First, the continuous growth in qubit counts has rendered distributed QCA inevitable, yet the non-deterministic latencies inherent in feedback loops demand cycle-accurate synchronization across multiple controllers. Existing synchronization strategies — whether lock-step or demand-driven — introduce significant performance penalties.

Here, we use unbiased screening to identify SARS-CoV-2 proteins...

pmc-10582391.title: Small interfering RNA–mediated allele-selective silencing of von Willebrand factor in vitro and in vivo
pmc-10582391.creator: Yvonne K Jongejan, Elisa Schrader Echeverri, Richard J Dirven, Kalina Paunovska, Noa A Linthorst, Annika de Jong, Johannes C Wellershoff, Kim D van der Gouw, Bart J M van Vlijmen, James E Dahlman, Jeroen C J Eikenboom
pmc-10582391.description: Key Points•Using 7C1 lipid nanoparticles, efficient endothelial delivery of siRNAs targeting VWF can be achieved.•Allele-selective silencing of VWF using siRNAs is feasible based on 1 nucleotide difference within mouse strains. Introduction Von Willebrand factor (VWF) is a multimeric plasma glycoprotein produced by endothelial cells and megakaryocytes.

pmc-10642725.title: Mosquito-borne flaviviruses and type I interferon: catch me if you can!
pmc-10642725.creator: Jim Zoladek, Sébastien Nisole
pmc-10642725.description: Mosquito-borne flaviviruses include many viruses that are important human pathogens, including Yellow fever virus, Dengue virus, Zika virus and West Nile virus. While these viruses have long been confined to tropical regions, they now pose a global public health concern, as the geographical distribution of their mosquito vectors has dramatically expanded.

pmc-11294293.title: Abdominal aneurysm sac thrombus CT density and volume after EVAR: which association with underlying endoleak?
pmc-11294293.creator: Matthias Lembrechts, Lucas Desauw, Walter Coudyzer, Annouschka Laenen, Inge Fourneau, Geert Maleux
pmc-11294293.description: BackgroundOur aim was to analyse abdominal aneurysm sac thrombus density and volume on computed tomography (CT) after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR).MethodsPatients who underwent EVAR between January 2005 and December 2010 and had at least four follow-up CT exams available over the first five years of follow-up were included in this retrospective single-centre study.

pmc-11396599.title: Challenges and Complications in the Management of Advanced Oropharyngeal Carcinoma: Role of Post-Mortem Diagnosis and Future Perspectives
pmc-11396599.creator: Francesca Consalvo, Matteo De Simone, Alfonso Scarpa, Alfonso Acerra, Francesco Antonio Salzano, Vittorio Fineschi, Alessandro Santurro, Maria Lina Tornesello
pmc-11396599.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Oropharyngeal squamous-cell carcinoma (OPSCC) poses significant challenges in diagnosis, treatment, and management and has important medico-legal and forensic implications. In particular, the management of OPSCC and its treatment-related complications can often be challenging. In cases with advanced OPSCC, a loco-regional extension of the tumor can contribute to the destruction of oral cavity tissues, while the radiotherapy treatment can induce profound changes in tissue morphology and structure.

pmc-11673269.title: Diabetic Glycation of Human Serum Albumin Affects Its Immunogenicity
pmc-11673269.creator: Cresci-Anne C C Croes, Marialena Chrysanthou, Tamara Hoppenbrouwers, Harry Wichers, Jaap Keijer, Huub F J Savelkoul, Malgorzata Teodorowicz, Maria Koziołkiewicz, Aleksandra Twarda-Clapa
pmc-11673269.description: Advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) are products of a non-enzymatic reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars. Glycated human serum albumin (HSA) increases in diabetics as a consequence of elevated blood glucose levels and glycating metabolites like methylglyoxal (MGO). The impact of different types of glycation on the immunomodulatory properties of HSA is poorly understood and is studied here.

pmc-12616083.title: Establishing a best practice for the freeze-thaw cycle of cryopreservation to approximate living muscle, joint, and associated soft tissue properties in cadaveric upper limbs
pmc-12616083.creator: Cade R McGarvey, Summer M Drees, Austin Lawrence, Noah D Miller, Sahil Kapur, Vihan De Silva, Martin Skie, Ahmed Suparno Bahar Moni
pmc-12616083.description: IntroductionFresh-frozen cadavers are useful for surgical simulation and experimentation since they preserve many properties of live specimens, but achieving realistic physiological properties requires thawing that risks tissue damage.MethodsTen fresh-frozen cadaveric upper limbs were frozen at −17 °C, refrigerated at 4 °C for 48 h, then thawed at room temperature for 8 h.

pmc-12718503.title: Oncoplastic or Conventional Breast-Conserving Surgery? Outcomes from a West Java Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-12718503.creator: Raden Yohana Azhar, Birgitta M Dewayani, Zuldi Erdiansyah, Prapanca Nugraha, Arrayyan Muhammad, Ahmad Naufal Alfarisy
pmc-12718503.description: PurposeBreast-conserving surgery (BCS) followed by adjuvant radiotherapy is the standard treatment for early breast cancer in Indonesia. Our aim was to compare the outcomes of BCS with oncoplastic surgery (OPS), a less common method of breast cancer treatment in the country.Patients and MethodsThis retrospective cohort study was conducted at Hasan Sadikin General Hospital, Bandung, West Java, Indonesia.

pmc-13317554.title: Chiral‐Encoded Pt‐Ir Surfaces as Apparent Spin Filter for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction
pmc-13317554.creator: Zikkawas Pasom, Krissanapat Yomthong, Sopon Butcha, Jonas Fransson, Chularat Wattanakit, Alexander Kuhn
pmc-13317554.description: Chiral Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) is a promising effect for enhancing the electrochemical oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), an essential process in clean energy technologies. So far, the concept has been validated mostly for surfaces modified with chiral organic layers; however, it remains unexplored for chiral metal matrices.

pmc-13627051.title: Psychometric properties of the Turkish version of the Flexible or Rigid Control of Eating Scale in women
pmc-13627051.creator: Çağdaş Salih Meriç, Mustafa Özgür, Emre Duman, Hacı Ömer Yılmaz
pmc-13627051.description: BackgroundEating control is a central construct in eating disorder research; however, existing measures often insufficiently capture its multidimensional nature and rarely distinguish rigid and flexible regulatory styles. The Flexible or Rigid Control of Eating Scale (FORCES) was developed to address this limitation; however, no culturally adapted instrument assessing rigid and flexible eating control has previously been validated in Turkish populations.

pmc-13659898.title: Cerebellar Ataxia, Neuropathy, and Vestibular Areflexia Syndrome (CANVAS): A case report of RFC1-associated disease
pmc-13659898.creator: Dhanush Amin, Raman Deep, Vidhi Dhaduk, Riyaz Ahmed FK, Jay Kakadiya
pmc-13659898.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cerebellar ataxia, neuropathy, and vestibular areflexia syndrome (CANVAS) is a late-onset neurodegenerative disorder associated with biallelic RFC1 repeat expansions. We report a 55-year-old woman with progressive imbalance, sensory neuronopathy, bilateral vestibular hypofunction, chronic cough, and orthostatic symptoms. MRI demonstrated cerebellar atrophy involving the vermis, particularly the posterior vermis, with additional involvement of the posterosuperior cerebellar hemispheres, including Crus I, and upper cervical spinal cord atrophy.
